RA_7581_Sec_6.text: Section 6. Automatic Price Control. — Unless otherwise declared by the President, prices of basic necessities in an area shall automatically be frozen at their prevailing prices or placed under automatic price control whenever that area is proclaimed or declared a disaster area or under a state of calamity. If the prevailing price of any basic necessity is excessive or unreasonable, the implementing agency may recommend to the President the imposition of a price ceiling. Unless sooner lifted by the President, price control of basic necessities under this section shall remain effective for the duration of the condition that brought it about, but not for more than sixty (60) days.

RA_10121_Sec_12.statute: Republic Act No. 10121 (Philippine Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act of 2010)
RA_10121_Sec_12.text: Section 12. Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (LDRRMO). — (a) There shall be established an LDRRMO in every province, city and municipality, and a Barangay Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Committee in every barangay which shall be responsible for setting the direction, development, implementation and coordination of disaster risk management programs within their territorial jurisdiction. (b) The LDRRMO shall be under the office of the governor or city or municipal mayor, and the BDRRMC shall be under the office of the punong barangay. The LDRRMOs shall be initially organized and composed of a Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Officer to be assisted by three staff responsible for administration, planning, and operations.

RA_11032_Sec_9.statute: Republic Act No. 11032 (Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Government Service Delivery Act of 2018)
RA_11032_Sec_9.text: Section 9(b)(1). Action of Offices. — All applications or requests submitted shall be acted upon by the assigned officer or employee within the prescribed processing time stated in the Citizen's Charter which shall not exceed: three (3) working days in the case of simple transactions; seven (7) working days in the case of complex transactions; and twenty (20) working days in the case of applications or requests involving activities which pose danger to public health, public safety, public morals, public policy, and highly technical transactions. The maximum time prescribed above may be extended only once for the same number of days, which shall be indicated in the Citizen's Charter.

RA_10931_Sec_4.statute: Republic Act No. 10931 (Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education Act)
RA_10931_Sec_4.text: Section 4. Free Higher Education in SUCs and LUCs. — All Filipino students who are enrolled in courses leading to a bachelor's degree or comparable undergraduate degree in State Universities and Colleges (SUCs) and Local Universities and Colleges (LUCs) shall be exempt from paying tuition and other school fees for units enrolled in: Provided, That they pass the entrance examination and other admission and retention requirements of the SUCs and LUCs. SUCs and LUCs shall not collect mandatory tuition or administrative fees from qualified undergraduate students, and the required funding shall be subsidized by the national government through annual appropriations.

RA_9165_Sec_36c.statute: Republic Act No. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002)
RA_9165_Sec_36c.text: Section 36(c). Authorized Drug Testing for Students. — Authorized drug testing shall be done by any government forensic laboratories or by any of the drug testing laboratories accredited and monitored by the Department of Health (DOH) to safeguard the quality of test results. Students of secondary and tertiary schools shall, pursuant to the related rules and regulations as contained in the school's student handbook and with notice to the parents, undergo a random drug testing: Provided, That all drug testing expenses whether in public or private schools under this Section will be borne by the government.

RA_11314_Sec_5.statute: Republic Act No. 11314 (Student Fare Discount Act)
RA_11314_Sec_5.text: Section 5. Student Fare Discount Privilege. — A student under this Act shall be entitled to a grant for twenty percent (20%) discount on the regular domestic transportation utility fares for land, rail, sea and air, upon presentation of their duly issued school identification cards or valid enrollment documents. The discount shall be granted across all public transportation utilities operating within Philippine territory throughout the entire calendar year.

RA_7160_Sec_458.statute: Republic Act No. 7160 (The Local Government Code of 1991)
RA_7160_Sec_458.text: Section 458(a)(1)(iii). Curfew and Public Order Powers. — (a) The sangguniang panlungsod, as the legislative body of the city, shall enact ordinances, approve resolutions and appropriate funds for the general welfare of the city and its inhabitants, and in the proper exercise of the corporate powers of the city, shall: (1) Approve ordinances and pass resolutions to protect the general welfare of the city and its inhabitants, and in pursuit thereof shall: (iii) Enact curfew ordinances regulating the movement and presence of minors during late-night hours, and adopt appropriate preventive measures to protect youth from juvenile delinquency.

RA_9344_Sec_6.statute: Republic Act No. 9344 (Juvenile Justice and Welfare Act of 2006)
RA_9344_Sec_6.text: Section 6. Minimum Age of Criminal Responsibility. — A child fifteen (15) years of age or under at the time of the commission of the offense shall be exempt from criminal liability. However, the child shall be subjected to an intervention program pursuant to Section 20 of this Act. A child above fifteen (15) years but below eighteen (18) years of age shall likewise be exempt from criminal liability and be subjected to an intervention program, unless he/she has acted with discernment, in which case, such child shall be subjected to the appropriate proceedings in accordance with this Act.

RA_7160_Sec_152c.statute: Republic Act No. 7160 (The Local Government Code of 1991)
RA_7160_Sec_152c.text: Section 152(c). Barangay Clearance. — No city or municipality may issue any license or permit for any business or activity unless a clearance is first obtained from the barangay where such business or activity is located or conducted. For such clearance, the sangguniang barangay may impose a reasonable fee. The application for clearance shall be acted upon within seven (7) working days from the filing thereof. In the event that the clearance is not issued within the said period, the city or municipality may issue the said license or permit.

RA_4136_Sec_35.statute: Republic Act No. 4136 (Land Transportation and Traffic Code)
RA_4136_Sec_35.text: Section 35. Restriction as to speed. — (a) Any person driving a motor vehicle on a highway shall drive the same at a careful and prudent speed, not greater nor less than is reasonable and proper. (b) Subject to the provisions of the preceding paragraph, the rate of speed of any motor vehicle shall not exceed the following: on open country roads with no blind corners, eighty (80) km. per hour for passenger cars and motorcycles, and fifty (50) km. per hour for motor trucks and buses; on through streets or boulevards, forty (40) km. per hour; on city and municipal streets with light traffic, thirty (30) km. per hour; and through crowded streets, twenty (20) km. per hour. (c) The rates of speed herein prescribed shall not apply to emergency medical vehicles, fire department vehicles, or law enforcement officers pursuing traffic violators.

RA_7925_Sec_4.statute: Republic Act No. 7925 (Public Telecommunications Policy Act of 1995)
RA_7925_Sec_4.text: Section 4. Declaration of National Policy. — Telecommunications is essential to the economic development, integrity and security of the Philippines, and as such shall be developed and administered as to safeguard, enrich and strengthen the economic, cultural, social and political fabric of the Philippines. A fundamental objective of government is to develop and maintain a viable, efficient, reliable and universally accessible telecommunications infrastructure. The expansion of telecommunications services shall be undertaken primarily by the private sector, and the entry and operation of telecommunications public utilities shall be regulated and supervised by the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC) as an independent administrative body pursuant to national policy.

RA_9136_Sec_43u.statute: Republic Act No. 9136 (Electric Power Industry Reform Act of 2001)
RA_9136_Sec_43u.text: Section 43(u). Functions of the Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC). — The ERC shall have the original and exclusive jurisdiction over all cases contesting rates, fees, fines and penalties imposed in the exercise of its powers, functions and responsibilities, and over all cases involving disputes between and among participants or players in the energy sector. All actions shall be within the exclusive jurisdiction of the Commission, and local government units shall not modify, alter, or superimpose additional local retail tariff rates upon distribution utilities licensed by the Commission.

RA_11223_Sec_6.statute: Republic Act No. 11223 (Universal Health Care Act)
RA_11223_Sec_6.text: Section 6. Service Coverage. — (a) Every Filipino shall be granted immediate eligibility and access to preventive, promotive, curative, rehabilitative, and palliative care for medical, dental, mental and emergency health services, delivered either as population-based or individual-based health services. (b) PhilHealth and the Department of Health (DOH), in coordination with local government units (LGUs), shall endeavor to provide a primary health care delivery system that will afford every Filipino access to a licensed primary care provider of choice without financial hardship at the point of service.

RA_11332_Sec_9.statute: Republic Act No. 11332 (Mandatory Reporting of Notifiable Diseases and Health Events of Public Health Concern Act)
RA_11332_Sec_9.text: Section 9. Prohibited Acts. — The following shall be prohibited under this Act: (a) Unauthorized disclosure of private and confidential information pertaining to a patient's medical condition or treatment; (b) Non-cooperation of persons and entities that should report and/or respond to notifiable diseases or health events of public health concern; and (c) Non-cooperation of the person or firms categorized as having the notifiable disease, or affected by the health event of public concern.

RA_9211_Sec_5.statute: Republic Act No. 9211 (Tobacco Regulation Act of 2003)
RA_9211_Sec_5.text: Section 5. Smoking in Public Places. — Smoking shall be absolutely prohibited in the following public places: (a) Centers of youth activity such as playschools, elementary schools, high schools, colleges and universities, youth hostels and recreational facilities for persons under eighteen (18) years old; (b) Elevators and stairwells; (c) Locations in which fire hazards are present, including gas stations and storage areas for flammable materials; (d) Within the buildings and premises of public and private hospitals, medical, dental, and optical clinics, health centers, nursing homes, dispensaries and laboratories; and (e) Public conveyances and public facilities.

RA_7942_Sec_70.statute: Republic Act No. 7942 (Philippine Mining Act of 1995)
RA_7942_Sec_70.text: Section 70. Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA). — Except during the exploration period of a mineral agreement or permit, an environmental clearance certificate shall be required based on an environmental impact assessment and procedures under the Philippine Environmental Impact Statement System including Sections 26 and 27 of the Local Government Code of 1991 which require prior consultation with affected communities and local government units.

RA_8550_Sec_18.statute: Republic Act No. 8550 (The Philippine Fisheries Code of 1998)
RA_8550_Sec_18.text: Section 18. Users of Municipal Waters. — All fishery related activities in municipal waters, as defined in this Code, shall be utilized by municipal fisherfolk and their cooperatives who are listed in the registry of municipal fisherfolk. The municipal or city government may, through its local chief executive and acting pursuant to an appropriate ordinance, permit small and medium commercial fishing vessels to operate within the ten point one (10.1) to fifteen (15) kilometer area from the shoreline in municipal waters, provided, that no commercial fishing is allowed in waters with depth less than seven (7) fathoms, and prior public consultation with the FARMC has been conducted.

RA_10591_Sec_31.statute: Republic Act No. 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act)
RA_10591_Sec_31.text: Section 31. Absence of Permit to Carry Outside of Residence. — The penalty of prision correccional and a fine of Ten thousand pesos (P10,000.00) shall be imposed upon any person who is licensed to own a firearm but who shall carry the registered firearm outside his/her residence without any legal permit to carry issued by the Chief of the Philippine National Police (PNP).

RA_7160_Sec_287.statute: Republic Act No. 7160 (The Local Government Code of 1991)
RA_7160_Sec_287.text: Section 287. Local Development Projects. — Each local government unit shall appropriate in its annual budget no less than twenty percent (20%) of its annual internal revenue allotment for local development projects. Copies of each local development plan shall be furnished the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG).

RA_10121_Sec_21.statute: Republic Act No. 10121 (Philippine Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act of 2010)
RA_10121_Sec_21.text: Section 21. Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF). — Not less than five percent (5%) of the estimated revenue from regular sources shall be set aside as the LDRRMF to support disaster risk management activities. Of the amount appropriated for LDRRMF, thirty percent (30%) shall be allocated as Quick Response Fund (QRF) or stand-by fund for relief and recovery programs in order that living conditions in communities stricken by disasters may be normalized as quickly as possible. Unexpended LDRRMF shall accrue to a special trust fund solely for the purpose of supporting disaster risk reduction activities within the next five (5) years.

RA_7160_Sec_233.statute: Republic Act No. 7160 (The Local Government Code of 1991)
RA_7160_Sec_233.text: Section 233. Rates of Levy on Real Property Tax. — A province or city or a municipality within the Metropolitan Manila Area shall fix a uniform rate of basic real property tax applicable to their respective localities as follows: (a) In the case of a province, at the rate not exceeding one percent (1%) of the assessed value of real property; and (b) In the case of a city or a municipality within the Metropolitan Manila Area, at the rate not exceeding two percent (2%) of the assessed value of real property.

RA_7160_Sec_140.statute: Republic Act No. 7160 (The Local Government Code of 1991)
RA_7160_Sec_140.text: Section 140. Amusement Tax. — (a) The province or city may levy an amusement tax to be collected from the proprietors, lessees, or operators of theaters, cinemas, concert halls, circuses, boxing stadia, and other places of amusement at a rate of not more than thirty percent (30%) of the gross receipts from admission fees. (c) The holding of operas, concerts, dramas, recitals, painting and art exhibitions, flower shows, musical programs, literary and oratorical presentations, except pop, rock, or similar concerts shall be exempt from the payment of the tax hereon imposed.
